newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia end-Sept palm oil stocks seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia end-Sept palm oil stocks seen higher.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil stocks are expected to be around 1.01 million tonnes at end-September 1997 from a revised 894,000 tonnes at end-September in 1996, the U.S. embassy said in its latest report.

"With a better than expected increase in crude palm oil (CPO) output, we anticipate the palm oil stock level to increase to about the one million tonnes level by the end of September," the embassy said.
It did not give an estimate for end-June stocks. But local traders estimated end-June stocks at around 795,000 tonnes.
The U.S. embassy also said Malaysian CPO production in the third quarter was estimated at 2.38 million tonnes against a revised 2.40 million tonnes in the same period of 1996.

"The industry is expecting CPO production to be marginally lower during June," the embassy said. A Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong on Monday projected output in June at 780,000 tonnes over May's 790,640 tonnes. The embassy said anticipation of bigger output in the coming months and weaker demand resulted in a fall in prices last month.
"The average monthly CPO price for June was 1,212 ringgit a tonne compared with 1,315 ringgit in May," the embassy said. ($1 = 2.52 ringgit)
